solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rock musician with dope facing reporter's questions

parts.note: a charlie is a fool or dope in British slang

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the words, so what follows is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: questions beginning 'what's...?'

explanation.surface: A rock star with drugs about him faces a journalist's grilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs, but here it is a silly person. 'Facing' just places the dope before the questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Watts was the long-serving drummer of the Rolling Stones, a famous rock band.

clue.text: Special language surrounding meditation, one that attracts Tom?

definitions.note: a relative clause; read with the 'one' before it, which also supplies a letter

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose, so the language word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: cant is the jargon of a particular group
TM stands for Transcendental Meditation
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A jargon wrapped round meditation, and then a riddle about something that draws in Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T disguises a tomcat as a man's name. 'One' does double duty, giving the numeral and opening the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Catmint is a plant whose scent cats find irresistible, and a tom is a male cat.

clue.text: Contemporary ending to Ezra Pound poem

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of the poet's first name counts

parts.note: the last letter of Ezra
to lam is to beat or pound
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A modern way to close a poem by Ezra Pound, the American modernist poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Pound looks like the poet's surname but is a verb meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A la mode means in fashion, up to date, which is a sense of contemporary.

clue.text: Set and match! Party arranged finally for tennis champion

parts.note: a set or group of things is a lot
a tie is a match in a cup competition
a do is a party

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the last letter of arranged

explanation.surface: Tennis language, set and match, then a party organised for a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: Set and match look like tennis scoring, which fits the definition, but they are ordinary words for group and contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lottie Dod won the Wimbledon ladies' singles five times in the 1880s and 1890s.

clue.text: Capsized US recruit among the boatmen?

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, and in a down clue that turns the letters end to end
to be among something is to sit inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier tipped into the water among a boat crew.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition overlaps the wordplay: 'the' is fodder as well as part of 'the boatmen'. The container is built first, then the whole is turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen, so the boatmen together make one.

clue.text: As Premiership team's losing 2 — 1, support is constant?

indicators.note: losing two means two letters are dropped, here from the end of the club's name

parts.note: Arsenal is a London football club in the Premier League
the Roman numeral for one
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A football club losing 2-1 wonders whether its fans will stay loyal.
explanation.walkthrough: As looks like the conjunction but is the chemical symbol of the element. The score 2 – 1 splits into a deletion of two letters and the numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic, element number 33 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Previous head Tongan occasionally adopts exotic dress

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the kept letters enclose the garment
occasionally means every so often, so only alternate letters are kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of Tongan
a sari is a South Asian wrapped garment

explanation.surface: A former Tongan leader now and then wears foreign clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Tongan suggests the Pacific kingdom's rulers, but it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was an empress of Russia, a ruler from the past rather than the present.

clue.text: Challenger at bridge protects English town

parts.note: in bridge, North and South play against East and West
to shield is to protect

explanation.surface: A rival at the card table guards an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge the four players are named after compass points, so any one is a challenger to the pair opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: North Shields is a town on the north bank of the Tyne in north-east England.

clue.text: Old National Trust kiln powerless?

parts.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage charity
an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: An old heritage-site kiln with no electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powerless' looks like a kiln without electricity, but the idiom 'to have someone on toast' means to have them at your mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone on toast is a British idiom for having them helpless and in your control.

clue.text: Light jabber hit softly

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
to lam is to hit
p, piano, is the musical mark for soft

explanation.surface: Someone gently strikes a light chatterer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas lamp is a lamp burning gas, the source of street light before electricity.

clue.text: One's played a bit before game against the French

parts.note: a bit is a coin, here a penny
whist is a card game
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone plays a little before a game against the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' only means next to: the French article sits beside the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A penny whistle is a cheap simple flute, so it is an instrument that gets played.

clue.text: Mind-blowing experience Colin uncovered somewhere on the Med

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go

parts.note: a trip is a hallucinogenic drug experience
the name, with its first and last letters about to go

explanation.surface: Colin has a mind-blowing time somewhere on the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital of Libya, a port city on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Spanish agreed to enter joint conflict

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: a tenon is the projecting part of a woodworking joint
si is Spanish for yes

explanation.surface: Spain agrees to join a combined conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like an adjective with conflict, but it is a carpentry joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is strained relations between parties, a state of conflict short of open fighting.

clue.text: French barman perhaps gave it a shake, partly on counter

indicators.note: counter means running the opposite way, so the letters are read right to left
partly means only a portion of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: letters spanning gavE IT A Shake

explanation.surface: A French bartender shakes a cocktail on the bar counter.
explanation.walkthrough: A composer writes music in bars, so he is a 'barman'; the cocktail-shaker picture is pure misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer, and a composer is jokingly a man of musical bars.

clue.text: Government protest changing crux of medieval battle

indicators.note: the crux is the central point, so the middle letter of the battle is swapped for another

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
Crecy was a 1346 battle of the Hundred Years' War

explanation.surface: A protest alters the key point of a medieval battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle E of the battle becomes A; 'crux' here means the centre letter rather than the decisive issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Democracy is a system of government by elected representatives of the people.

clue.text: Horse around in Liverpool water, avoiding unknown river diver

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the water's name
an unknown in algebra is x, y or z, and avoiding it means dropping that letter

parts.note: the Mersey is the river at Liverpool

indicators.note: turning around makes the animal word read backwards

parts.note: a nag is a horse
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A horse in the Mersey steers clear of a strange river diver.
explanation.walkthrough: Y is dropped from MERSEY, then the turned horse goes inside and R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A merganser is a fish-eating duck that dives underwater to catch its prey.

clue.text: Data latterly ignored one senior baseball player

indicators.note: ignoring the latter part means the final letter is left off

parts.note: info, information, is data
the Roman numeral for one
an elder is a senior person

explanation.surface: Records of a veteran baseball player were later disregarded.
explanation.definitionFit: An infielder plays one of the positions around the bases in baseball.

clue.text: Exchange amorous petting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the nickname of the FTSE 100 share index of the London Stock Exchange
second meaning: flirtatious touching of feet under a table

explanation.surface: Swapping romantic caresses.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Financial Times the stock market sense is home ground; the FTSE index is pronounced like the flirting game.
explanation.definitionFit: The FTSE index is spoken of as the Footsie, and playing footsie is secret flirtation with feet.

clue.text: Devious sinner claiming payment card that's turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters run bottom to top
claiming means taking hold of, so the sinner wraps round the card

parts.note: Eve was the first sinner in Genesis
Visa is a payment card brand

explanation.surface: A crooked wrongdoer claims with a credit card that was found.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasive behaviour avoids straight answers, which is shifty and devious.

clue.text: Warmer, relative to Hebrides at first

parts.note: bro is short for brother

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letters of the words before it

parts.note: first letters of to and Hebrides

explanation.surface: A warmer garment for a relative heading to the Hebrides, the Scottish islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warmer' looks like a comparative adjective but is a noun: something that warms you.
explanation.definitionFit: Broth is a hot soup, the kind of thing that warms a person on a cold day.

clue.text: Packet pasty, in middle, hot air

parts.note: a packet and a bomb both mean a large sum of money

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters, leaving off both ends

parts.note: the middle three letters of pasty

explanation.surface: A packaged pasty, hot in the middle and full of air.
explanation.walkthrough: A packet and a bomb are both British slang for a lot of money, as in 'it cost a bomb'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombast is pompous, inflated talk with little substance, which is hot air.

clue.text: Former ace that waits for no man?

parts.note: an ace counts as one in cards
from the proverb time and tide wait for no man

explanation.surface: A former champion who waits for nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: One-time is an adjective meaning former, as in a one-time champion.

clue.text: Penny switches to tango in spotted thing that dancer often wears

definitions.note: a clause describing the garment; read it as 'thing that dancer often wears'

indicators.note: switching one thing to another is a swap, one letter replaced by another

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny
Tango is T in the NATO alphabet
the leopard is the big cat famous for its spots

explanation.surface: A dancer changes a penny to tango in a spotty outfit she often wears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thing' does double duty, completing the spotted animal and the worn garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is a close-fitting one-piece garment worn by dancers and gymnasts.

clue.text: Small drink to overcome a crisis

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wee nip to get through a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'overcome' puts the drink on top of the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is an exciting or troubling turn of events, a crisis in everyday speech.

clue.text: Stray addict's opening declaration of inferiority?

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of addict
saying 'I'm less' admits being inferior

explanation.surface: An addict, drifting, begins by confessing he feels inferior.
explanation.definitionFit: Stray as an adjective means wandering or random, so it is close to aimless, having no purpose.

clue.text: Son getting money in the main for poetic style

indicators.note: in puts the son with his cash inside the word for the sea

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
S is the abbreviation for son
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A son making money at sea, all for the sake of a poetic form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting' joins son and money before both go inside SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestina is a verse form of six six-line stanzas that rotate the same end words.

clue.text: Dog having picked up garland, snoozes

indicators.note: picking something up lifts it, and the letters are taken in the opposite order

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
naps are snoozes

explanation.surface: A dog that has fetched a garland dozes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts a sound-alike reading; here it turns the words garland and snoozes backwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaniel is a breed of gun dog with long drooping ears.

clue.text: Artist's cleaning procedure, with spirit, seen in Irish media

indicators.note: to be seen in something is to be inside it, so the station's name goes round

parts.note: RTE is Ireland's national broadcaster
an enema flushes out the bowels
grit is courage or spirit

explanation.surface: An Irish broadcaster shows an artist's cleaning routine, carried out with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests turpentine for cleaning brushes, but it means courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Rene Magritte was a Belgian surrealist painter, famous for the pipe that is not a pipe.
